21. (New) A therapeutic training device comprising a head mounted display having an outward facing video display comprising a transparency that is variable, and further comprising a light having an adjustable brightness to illuminate the eyes of a wearer.
22. (New) The therapeutic training device of claim 21, comprising a controller configured to inversely adjust the transparency of the outward facing video display and the brightness of the light.
23. (New) The therapeutic training device of claim 21, wherein the outward facing video display a video projector, a LCD display, a LED display, or a quantum dot display.
24. (New) The therapeutic training device of claim 21, wherein the outward facing video display comprises a plurality of outward facing video displays.
25. (New) The therapeutic training device of claim 21, comprising eye tracking components and software.
26. (New) The therapeutic training device of claim 21, comprising a controller configured to adjust a transparency of the outward facing video display, and adjust the brightness of the light.
27. (New) A therapeutic training device, comprising:
eyeglass frames;
an outward facing video display positioned within the eyeglass frames; and
a controller coupled to the outward facing video display to control a display of media content on the video display, such that the display of media content is viewable by a patient with the therapeutic training device is worn by a user.
28. (New) The device of claim 27, wherein the outward facing video display is a video projector, a LCD display, a LED display, or a quantum dot display.
29. (New) The device of claim 27, wherein the outward facing video display comprises a plurality of outward facing video displays.
30. (New) The device of claim 27, comprising a light having an adjustable brightness to illuminate the eyes of the user.
31. (New) The device of claim 27, wherein a transparency of the media content displayed on the outward facing video display is adjustable.
32. (New) The device of claim 31, wherein the transparency of the media content displayed on the outward facing video display is adjusted manually by the user.
33. (New) The device of claim 31, wherein the transparency of the media content displayed on the outward facing video display is adjusted by software.
34. (New) The device of claim 27, comprising eye tracking components and software.
35. (New) The device of claim 27, wherein a transparency of the media content displayed on the outward facing video display is variable, and wherein the device further comprises a light having an adjustable brightness and configured to illuminate, wherein a brightness of the light is adjustable to illuminate the eyes of the user.
36. (New) The device of claim 35, comprising a controller configured to inversely adjust a transparency of the outward facing video display and the brightness of the light.
